title: Local Minimax Estimation of Both-Arm Susceptibility in Crossover Trials with Rare Counts
banked_reason: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: GuSilverman2026 publicly announces ZIP minimax-risk and confidence-set-size bounds but exposes no theorem, target, or class, so the decisive priority comparison and a field-level advance are not supported.

proof_attempt_summary: The proposal developed a positive-neighborhood local-minimax frontier for the both-arm-susceptible mass in a rare-count crossover model. One bounded revision repaired the oracle-center coherence and triangular-array well-posedness defects, after which the reviewer cleared soundness but repeated the same novelty defect: unavailable theorem-level Gu–Silverman material prevents a decisive priority comparison and therefore a field-tier claim. The mathematical formulation remains reusable for a future re-raise if theorem-level prior-work evidence becomes available or a genuinely new field-scale extension is proved.
tldr: In a randomized two-period crossover satisfying stable binary susceptibility, no carryover, homogeneous Poisson emissions, and conditional independence, how accurately can one estimate the both-arm susceptibility mass \(p_{11}\) when counts are rare? The proposed oracle-center local minimax theorem has squared risk \((p_{11}^{\star})^2\) times a clipped sum of inverse co-positive and two within-arm calibration scales, with constants uniform over feasible center face configurations and rate imbalance. It also seeks a center-aware confidence-width order, a distinct center-free exact-coverage interval, and same-law causal-assumption counterexamples. First-discovery priority remains uncertified.
gap: The existing BZIP model and positive-count calibration results do not determine the center-aware full-simplex triangular-array risk and width of the joint mass \(p_{11}\). A related public Hwang–Stoklosa–Chen preprint supplies marginal-occupancy theorem text; the Gu–Silverman ZIP minimax abstract does not expose its target or theorem, leaving direct priority uncertain.
fill: Investigate finite-sample oracle-center risk and honest-width frontiers with explicit positive rare array criteria, a separate center-free exact-coverage procedure, and scoped same-law causal audits. The intended result is a focused contribution; field-level priority and reach are not yet established.
